newsitem.title: USA: US Plains feedlot cattle market inactive- feedlots.
newsitem.headline: US Plains feedlot cattle market inactive- feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle markets near midday Friday remained inactive, with no sales reported, feedlot sources said.
Light packer inquiry was noted at some feedyards following fairly active trade this week at $64.00 per cwt, down $1.00 from last week, they said.
Most of the cattle on this week's showlist were sold, and those left were underfinished and could use more days on feed, sources said.
Packers reportedly had sufficient inventory to get them into the middle of next week, cattle feeders said.
Texas Panhandle and western Oklahoma weekly volume was estimated by USDA at 93,000 head. The showlist had been pegged at 80,000 head, trade sources said.
Kansas weekly volume was 87,600 head, USDA said. The Kansas showlist this week was estimated near 78,000 head.
Beef prices at midday were higher for the first time since January 20, USDA statistics showed.

Beef prices were quoted up $0.12 to $0.43 per cwt, with 201 fabricated loads sold, USDA said. Choice lightweight beef was quoted up $0.43 at $97.32, compared with $103.14 on January 20, the last time prices were quoted higher.
